sedge noun

also marsh grass, reed-grass

classical

Verg. G. 3.231 (Lewis & Short)
Col. 11.2.62 (Lewis & Short)

cārex, cāricis f.

noun, third declension

sedge, reed-grass

Other words

  • ulva, ulvae f. — sedge, marsh grass

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Verg. G. 3.175 (Lewis & Short); Verg. E. 8.87 (Lewis & Short); Ov. Met. 6.345 (Lewis & Short); Cato Agr. 37.2 (Lewis & Short)

    The coarse grass of marshes and stream sides; botanists now use the name for a seaweed.

  • cārectum, cārectī n. — a bed of sedge

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Verg. E. 3.20 (Lewis & Short); Col. 6.22.2 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • frondibus hirsūtīs et cārice pāstus acūtā

    fed on shaggy leaves and sharp sedgeVerg. G. 3.231

  • propter aquae rīvum viridī prōcumbit in ulvā

    she sinks down by a stream of water in the green sedgeVerg. E. 8.87

  • nōn illīc canna palūstris nec sterilēs ulvae nec acūtā cuspide juncī

    there is no marsh reed there, no barren sedge, no sharp-pointed rushesOv. Met. 4.298–299

  • tū post cārecta latēbās

    you were hiding behind the sedgeVerg. E. 3.20

See also rush, reed, swamp, grass.
